title: De Umbris Idearum (Latin)
author: Giordano Bruno
description: De Umbris Idearum (On the Shadows of Ideas) by Giordano Bruno (1548-1600), the Dominican philosopher burned for heresy in Rome, in the Latin new edition edited by Salvatore Tugini (Berlin: E. S. Mittler, 1868). First published in Paris in 1582 and dedicated to King Henri III, it is Bruno's first major work on the art of memory. The first part presents a Neoplatonic and Hermetic metaphysics: all things are shadows of the divine ideas, and the human mind can ascend from shadows to the light. The second part sets out an extraordinarily elaborate mnemonic system based on rotating concentric wheels, inspired by Ramon Llull, combined with images of the decans, planets and mythological figures, intended to imprint the order of the cosmos on the imagination. Made famous by Frances Yates's studies, it is a key work of Renaissance Hermeticism and magical memory arts.
